steps.title: Finite morphisms preserve component dimension here
steps.text: A finite surjective map from an equidimensional finite-type field-scheme of dimension n has equidimensional target of dimension n. Indeed every source component has closed image with function-field extension finite and the same dimension; the finitely many images cover the target. A maximal irreducible subset of their union is one of these images. Thus every target component has dimension n and every source-component image is a target component. Apply this to the canonical reduction and formal special fibre in A3. In particular every original residual component Y of mathcalX has dimension n. This conclusion does not come from total degree or a Hilbert-polynomial leading coefficient. Every point over a generic Y is over a generic canonical component and hence is a Shilov point by GRW2.16. This recovers the precise generated assertion of GM A.3 without reversing the composition.

steps.title: Maximal residual dimension and generic ORIGINAL scheme support
steps.text: On that strictly C-affinoid chart take any such actual Shilov point y. The WHOLE Poineau2013 Lemma4.4 gives s_C(y)=dim_C,y(U)=n: isolate its residual component by a norm1 Laurent localization, inject its n-dimensional generic residue field into the residue of H(y), and use the upper Abhyankar inequality. The immediate printed proof, field conventions, and original page284 have now been read directly. To see generic scheme support in ORIGINAL X_C, no mere singleton-fibre assertion is used. H(y) is the completion of the valued scheme field kappa(xi) at xi=ker(y). Choose n independent residue classes in H(y), approximate their norm1 lifts in kappa(xi) with error<1, and retain the same residues. For a nonzero polynomial relation over C, divide its coefficient family by a coefficient of maximal norm; the nonzero reduced polynomial cannot vanish on these independent residues. Thus the lifts are algebraically independent over C. Hence trdeg_C kappa(xi)>=n. On an integral n-dimensional finite-type C-variety only its generic point has dimension n. Therefore xi is the original generic point and H(y) is the completion of honest C(X).

steps.title: ONE original-field section nonzero at all residual components
steps.text: There are finitely many residual components because the model is quasi-compact with finite-type residual charts. At each generic residual point at least one original S_l is nonzero, by actual global generation of mathcalM. The bad coefficient vectors lambda in the original residue-field vector space whose combination vanishes at that point form a proper linear subspace: a standard basis vector corresponding to a nonzero S_l is outside it, even though the component field is an extension of the original residue field. The original residue field is infinite in characteristic0. A finite union of proper linear subspaces does not cover a finite-dimensional vector space over an infinite field: choose a line direction and translate avoiding the finitely many whole-line obstructions, then avoid finitely many intersection parameters. Choose lambda avoiding all these kernels and lift its entries to K-circle. At least one entry is a unit, so elementary integral row operations complete this row to an invertible matrix over K-circle. The inverse matrix is integral too. The old and new section families have identical maximum norms at every analytic point by the two non-Archimedean triangle inequalities. Thus theta and the same original very ample embedding bundle remain EXACTLY unchanged. Rename the combination S0. Its model norm is1 at every selected y_i; all new g_l=S_l/S0 have norm<=1 there.

steps.title: Residual COORDINATE subfield has full dimension
steps.text: On the original projective-closure chart S0!=0, its special coordinate algebra is generated over C-tilde by the residue classes of the ORIGINAL g_l. The finite p_s maps each n-dimensional component Y of mathcalX_s finitely onto a closed integral image Z in mathcalX0_s, preserving dimension n. Equivalently the inclusion of its image coordinate algebra into the component coordinate algebra has finite fraction-field extension kappa(Z)->kappa(Y). Thus the coordinate subfield C-tilde(bar g_1,...,bar g_N)=kappa(Z) has transcendence degree n. The reduction-kernel definition injects kappa(Y), and therefore this subfield, into H(y_i)-tilde. On this open chart y_i reduces to the generic point, so those coordinate residues are exactly the residue classes of g_l(y_i). No claim that this subfield is all of H(y_i)-tilde is needed. A5 gives independently that the latter whole field has transcendence degree n. These are precisely the THREE initial point hypotheses of native243.
